topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Cancer as clonal evolution shaped by mutations and its microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an evolutionary process in which mutations and the cellular context together shape the development of invasive growths.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and the debate over cancer risk and bad luck
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and challenge the idea that cancer is simply a matter of bad luck.

topics.label: Geographical cancer patterns as evidence of environmental and genetic influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics use differences in cancer rates across populations to examine how environment and inherited predisposition may influence cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development, including Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to cancer and use Burkitt lymphoma to show how infectious and other factors can combine in its development.

topics.label: How environmental agents cause DNA damage and mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how exposures can damage DNA directly or after processing in the body, leading to mutations and, in some cases, tissue-specific effects.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and context-dependent susceptibility to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show that cancer development depends not only on mutations but also on promoting conditions and biological contexts that affect whether susceptible cells grow into tumours.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for identifying carcinogenic exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe ways to infer exposure to carcinogens and assess their carcinogenic potential using evidence from cancer genomes, populations, animals, and laboratory assays.

topics.label: Lecture closing: summary and cancer risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing decisions about carcinogens as a balance of risks and benefits.
